canonical.title: Construct BST from Preorder Traversal
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/08. Build BST from Preorder Traversal.cpp

narrative.title: Rebuilding the Route Hierarchy from the Departure Log
narrative.scenario: A courier network's dispatcher kept only one log: every hub recorded the moment it was opened, before any of its branches. Because each hub's opening value also fixed the boundary its branches could not cross, the whole hierarchy can be rebuilt by replaying the log with running limits — a value beyond the current hub's ceiling belongs to some earlier hub's right wing instead.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array preorder — the preorder traversal (root, left subtree, right subtree) of a binary search tree with unique values.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the constructed BST serialized as a level-order array with trailing nulls trimmed.
constraints: All values are unique and a valid BST exists

testCases.explanation: 8 roots the tree; 1 and 7 hang under 5, and 10 gains the right child 12.
1 is below 2 and 3 is above it, giving a perfectly balanced root.

hintLevels: Level 1: The log opens each hub before its branches — the first value is always the current root.
Level 2: Carry an upper bound down the recursion; a value exceeding the bound closes this subtree and unwinds.
Level 3: One shared read cursor over the array makes the build single-pass O(n) — no searching for split points.
